Overnight Market Turmoil: International Oil Prices Plunge Over 8%, Gold Breaks Through $4,060, Chinese ADRs Rally Collectively
sum: Global financial markets experienced sharp swings overnight. International crude oil prices plunged more than 8% in a single session, gold and silver surged in tandem, the three major U.S. stock indexes closed higher but with severe internal divergence, and Chinese ADRs staged an independent strong rally. Meanwhile, the People's Bank of China announced a 300 billion yuan (approximately $45.0 billion) outright reverse repurchase operation, and a number of China A-share listed companies rolled out buyback and share increase plans in quick succession.

The oil market was the epicenter of this round of volatility. Traders bet that Middle East tensions could cool more quickly after the U.S. midterm elections. January-delivery Brent crude futures settled down 8.67% at $94.62 a barrel, while December-delivery WTI crude futures fell 8.29% to $88.12 a barrel. The scale of the single-day decline was rare for the energy market in recent memory.

Precious metals moved in the completely opposite direction. Spot gold rose 3.28% to $4,058.93 an ounce, while November-delivery COMEX gold futures gained 3.39% to $4,061.10 an ounce. Spot silver rose 4.86% to $52.19 an ounce, with COMEX silver futures up an even sharper 5.11%.

On the U.S. equities side, the Dow Jones Industrial Average closed up 3.03%, topping 53,000 points for the first time since September 8 and posting its best single-day performance since April 9, 2025. The Nasdaq Composite rose 1.44% and the S&P 500 gained 1.58%. But behind the index gains was a sharp rupture between sectors.

Large-cap technology stocks surged collectively, with Microsoft and Amazon both up more than 6% and Apple up 5.31%. In stark contrast, artificial intelligence and semiconductor-related names fell against the trend: Nvidia dropped 3.17%, the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 3.6% to a six-month low, and Marvell Technology tumbled more than 7%. Memory chip stocks were especially weak, with Seagate Technology down more than 8%, Micron Technology and SanDisk down 7%, and Western Digital down more than 6%. Cloud services company CoreWeave fell more than 9% and NEBIUS dropped more than 7%; in optical communications, Lumentum and Coherent each fell more than 5%.

Democrats' Midterm Gains Send Asian Chip Stocks Tumbling Before Rebound; Market Reprices AI Regulatory Risk
sum: Preliminary vote counts from the US midterm elections showed Democrats making larger-than-expected gains, putting the congressional power balance on course for a reshuffle, and markets promptly repriced the outlook for artificial intelligence regulation. During Asian trading on Nov. 4, chip stocks in South Korea, Japan and Taiwan fell sharply at one point, then narrowed losses markedly as investors digested what a "divided government" actually means. South Korea's KOSPI (Kospi) even swung from an intraday drop of 4% to nearly erasing all its losses.

According to NetEase, Democrats not only retook control of the House of Representatives but also won several key Senate seats and flipped traditional Republican strongholds including Texas, South Carolina and Kansas. The result briefly triggered a selloff in risk assets: Nasdaq 100 futures fell more than 2%, S&P 500 futures dropped over 1%, the Nikkei 225 fell more than 4% intraday, and the KOSPI's decline also widened to 4%.

Asian chip stocks were the epicenter of the swing. Shares of Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix each fell at least 4.5% intraday, becoming the main drags on the KOSPI. South Korea's stock market, previously seen as a barometer of Asia's AI trade, posted among the steepest declines among major Asian markets that day. The MSCI Asia-Pacific index fell as much as 2.3% intraday, led by the technology sector.

The core market concern is the regulatory path. Investors worry that Democratic control of Congress could push for tighter scrutiny of large technology companies and the AI industry, especially approvals for data center construction and energy policy. US data center expansion is a key source of orders for semiconductor and hardware suppliers in South Korea, Japan and Taiwan. If the pace of construction slows, demand expectations for high-performance memory chips and server-related components would come under direct pressure.

Huh Jae-Hwan, an analyst at South Korea's Eugene Investment & Securities, noted that elections in Ohio and Texas deserve particular attention because those two states are increasingly becoming important clusters for AI data center investment.

NetEase Golden Cross Formed: Stock Drops 6.53% (October 22, 2026)
sum: On October 22, 2026: price 181.80 HKD, trend sideways, RSI 39.6, support 180.90, resistance 199.10. technical analysis of netease stock.

NetEase fell 6.53% to HK$181.80 on October 22, putting the stock near its three-month low after a sharp session that was about 1.9 times its average daily trading range. The decline has brought it close to support, even as a recently formed golden cross—the 20-day average moving above the 50-day average—offers a counterpoint. The market is weighing a fragile short-term recovery signal against fresh evidence of selling pressure.

NetEase is trading below both its 20-day simple moving average (SMA) of HK$190.50 and its 50-day SMA of HK$190.00. That leaves the share price beneath a closely grouped band of potential resistance. The averages still show a golden cross, but the signal describes a recent change in the averages, not a guarantee that prices will keep rising. With the broader trend classified as sideways, the cross has yet to overcome the pull of the latest sell-off.

The share is now near the bottom of its 20-trading-day range, between support at HK$180.90 and resistance at HK$199.10. It is also close to the three-month low of HK$179.00. That proximity makes the next move around support particularly informative: holding there could suggest the sell-off is meeting buyers, while a break would put the three-month low into focus.

The momentum indicators are mixed, but their short-term message is cautious. RSI is 39.6, in neutral territory, below the level usually associated with an overbought market but not low enough to confirm that selling has become extreme. The Stochastic reading is more stretched: %K at 5.7 is below %D at 44.3, indicating an oversold condition. Oversold readings can accompany a rebound, but they can also persist while prices continue falling.

The MACD adds to that caution. Its histogram has turned negative at -0.240, while the MACD line at 0.957 sits below its signal line at 1.197. This suggests that near-term momentum has weakened even as the moving averages retain their golden cross. The signals are therefore not aligned: the cross reflects the earlier trend, while MACD captures the more recent loss of strength.

NETEASE CLOUD MUSIC AND gamma. ANNOUNCE NEW STRATEGIC PARTNERSHIP IN CHINA FOR MUSIC FROM YE, MARIAH CAREY, SEXYY RED, USHER, SNOOP DOGG AND MORE
sum: HANGZHOU, China and LOS ANGELES, Oct. 8, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- NetEase Cloud Music and gamma., the global media and technology company founded by Larry Jackson and Ike Youssef, today announced a multi-year strategic partnership that will expand opportunities for gamma.'s global artist roster in China while deepening NetEase Cloud Music's connection to international music and culture.

Under the new agreement, NetEase Cloud Music will serve as a key launch platform for licensed recordings from gamma.'s roster of leading artists, including Ye, Mariah Carey, Sexyy Red, Usher, Snoop Dogg, and more. Beyond music distribution, the partnership will create opportunities for collaboration across artist promotion, cultural exchange, original music content, and other initiatives designed to connect global artists with audiences in China.

The partnership builds on gamma.'s broader strategy of creating new pathways for artists to reach audiences, grow their businesses, and participate in culture across markets, while expanding NetEase Cloud Music's access to a diverse roster of internationally recognized and emerging artists. Together, the companies will explore new opportunities to amplify artists and music across borders, deepen connections between global artists and Chinese audiences, and foster greater cultural exchange.

In September 2025, Mariah Carey's latest album, Here For It All, made its China debut on NetEase Cloud Music, generating more than four times the volume of Carey's 2018 album Caution during its first two weeks. The album also delivered record-setting first-day streams and, by day 14, had surpassed every studio album Carey released in the previous decade in the China market.

The success of Here For It All demonstrates the potential of combining gamma.'s artist platform with NetEase Cloud Music's reach and market expertise. The expanded partnership formalizes that collaboration and establishes a broader framework for bringing gamma.'s artists to new audiences while creating new opportunities for NetEase Cloud Music to participate in the larger music ecosystem.

Are Options Traders Betting on a Big Move in NetEase Stock?
sum: Investors in NetEase, Inc. NTES need to pay close attention to the stock based on moves in the options market lately. That is because the Dec 18, 2026 $70 Call had some of the highest implied volatility of all equity options today.

Implied volatility shows how much movement the market is expecting in the future. Options with high levels of implied volatility suggest that investors in the underlying stocks are expecting a big move in one direction or the other. It could also mean there is an event coming up soon that may cause a big rally or a huge sell-off. However, implied volatility is only one piece of the puzzle when putting together an options trading strategy.

Clearly, options traders are pricing in a big move for NetEase shares, but what is the fundamental picture for the company? Currently, NetEase is a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) in the Internet - Software and Services industry that ranks in the Bottom 32% of our Zacks Industry Rank. Over the last 60 days, one analyst has increased the earnings estimate for the current quarter, while none have revised their estimates downward. The net effect has taken our Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current quarter from $2.26 per share to $2.39 in that period.

Given the way analysts feel about NetEase right now, this huge implied volatility could mean there's a trade developing. Oftentimes, options traders look for options with high levels of implied volatility to sell premium. This is a strategy many seasoned traders use because it captures decay. At expiration, the hope for these traders is that the underlying stock does not move as much as originally expected.

sum: On August 26, U.S. stock index futures diverged in premarket trading. Dow Jones Industrial Average futures edged up 0.1%, Nasdaq 100 futures slipped 0.21%, and S&P 500 futures dipped 0.07%. Hong Kong stocks closed the day on a more positive note. The Hang Seng Index finished up 0.56%, while the Hang Seng Tech Index gained 0.82%. Tech and semiconductor names showed clear structural divergence: XPeng Group surged nearly 8%, Hua Hong Semiconductor climbed over 6%, and NIO, SMIC (0981.HK), and Alibaba led the gainers. From a sector rotation perspective, the strength in Hong Kong-listed semiconductor and new energy vehicle names stood in sharp contrast to the premarket pullback in U.S. memory chip stocks. Notably, the Hang Seng Tech Index's gain significantly outpaced the broader Hang Seng Index, indicating that large-cap tech names were the primary driver of the day's upside in Hong Kong.

Does Entegris (ENTG) Have the Potential to Rally 26.18% as Wall Street Analysts Expect?
sum: Shares of Entegris (ENTG) have gained 9.4% over the past four weeks to close the last trading session at $138.25, but there could still be a solid upside left in the stock if short-term price targets of Wall Street analysts are any indication. Going by the price targets, the mean estimate of $174.45 indicates a potential upside of 26.2%.

The average comprises 11 short-term price targets ranging from a low of $120.00 to a high of $215.00, with a standard deviation of $23.71. While the lowest estimate indicates a decline of 13.2% from the current price level, the most optimistic estimate points to a 55.5% upside. More than the range, one should note the standard deviation here, as it helps understand the variability of the estimates. The smaller the standard deviation, the greater the agreement among analysts.

While the consensus price target is a much-coveted metric for investors, solely banking on this metric to make an investment decision may not be wise at all. That's because the ability and unbiasedness of analysts in setting price targets have long been questionable.

But, for ENTG, an impressive average price target is not the only indicator of a potential upside. Strong agreement among analysts about the company's ability to report better earnings than they predicted earlier strengthens this view. While a positive trend in earnings estimate revisions doesn't gauge how much a stock could gain, it has proven to be powerful in predicting an upside.

According to researchers at several universities across the globe, a price target is one of many pieces of information about a stock that misleads investors far more often than it guides. In fact, empirical research shows that price targets set by several analysts, irrespective of the extent of agreement, rarely indicate where the price of a stock could actually be heading.

While Wall Street analysts have deep knowledge of a company's fundamentals and the sensitivity of its business to economic and industry issues, many of them tend to set overly optimistic price targets. Are you wondering why?
They usually do that to drum up interest in shares of companies that their firms either have existing business relationships with or are looking to be associated with.

NetEase Cloud Music Defends Its Final Music Market Share Against Qishui Music Competition
sum: NetEase Cloud Music does not want to let Qishui Music snatch away its last note.

In 2013, when NetEase Cloud Music first broke into the sky of China's digital music market, Tencent Music had already built a solid moat with its huge copyright empire. On the frontal battlefield of the copyright war, NetEase Cloud Music barely had any chance of winning.

However, NetEase Cloud Music opened up a differentiated path: community and algorithm. The organic integration of the three major functions — playlists, comment sections, and private FM — allowed NetEase Cloud Music to bypass copyright barriers and directly tap into the younger generation's demand for "music roaming" in their spiritual world.

This set of strategies was all the rage in the mid-to-late 2010s. The unique "Cloud Village" culture built extremely high user stickiness among young people, and the term "NetEase Depression Cloud" once evolved from a joke to a cultural symbol. The story sharing and emotional resonance in the late-night comment sections constituted the most unique brand spiritual asset of NetEase Cloud Music.

However, the tide of the era has finally crossed the inflection point. This barrier built on textual sentiment and static recommendation is being diluted by ByteDance's Qishui Music, and NetEase Cloud Music is obviously unwilling to surrender.

On August 20, NetEase Cloud Music released its financial report for the first half of 2026. The financial report shows that total revenue in the first half of 2026 was 3.959 billion yuan, a year-on-year increase of 3.40%; net profit was 809 million yuan, a year-on-year decrease of 57%; gross profit was 1.474 billion yuan, a year-on-year increase of 5.9%.

NetEase shares fall as Q2 earnings miss overshadows stronger revenue
sum: NetEase (NASDAQ:NTES) shares dropped more than 5% in U.S. premarket trading on Thursday after the Chinese gaming and internet group reported second-quarter earnings that fell substantially short of analyst forecasts, outweighing better-than-expected revenue growth.

The company posted earnings per share of RMB12.02, well below the consensus estimate of RMB15.54. Revenue provided a more positive signal, increasing 7.9% year on year to RMB30.11 billion and beating analysts' expectations of RMB29.48 billion.
NetEase's core games and related value-added services division remained the main driver of growth, generating net revenue of RMB25.0 billion during the quarter.
That represented an increase of 9.7% from the corresponding period last year, reinforcing the importance of gaming to the group's overall financial performance.
Youdao also delivered growth, with net revenue increasing 3.5% year on year to RMB1.5 billion.
Performance elsewhere was more subdued. NetEase Cloud Music generated approximately RMB2.0 billion in net revenue, broadly unchanged from a year earlier.
Revenue from innovative businesses and other operations declined 3.5% to RMB1.6 billion.

sum: Alibaba and NetEase both report earnings the same morning, forcing a direct choice between two very different China tech bets. Analyst sentiment, price targets, and crowd prediction markets all point in conflicting directions, and only one stock survives the growth…

Alibaba (NYSE:BABA | BABA Price Prediction) and NetEase (NASDAQ:NTES) both step onto the earnings stage before the open on Thursday, August 20, 2026, with Alibaba reporting fiscal Q1 2027 and NetEase reporting Q2 2026. This simultaneous reporting gives investors a real choice for a growth allocation: the AI and cloud reinvestment story or the cash-generative gaming franchise. For a growth-oriented investor, which stock is more attractive ahead of the report?

The sell side is heavily bullish on both, but the degree differs. Alibaba shows 8 Strong Buy, 30 Buy, one Hold, no Sell, and one Strong Sell ratings, with 95% bullish sentiment and 3% bearish. NetEase counts 6 Strong Buy, 25 Buy, one Hold, and zero Sell ratings, with 97% bullish sentiment and 0% bearish. Alibaba last traded at $128.15, compared with an analyst target of $189.73 and a 24/7 Wall St. model base case of $157.65, implying 23.0% upside, with a 0.9 confidence score. NetEase closed at $124.75, compared with a $161.82 analyst target and a 24/7 Wall St. model target of $151.67, implying 21.58% upside at 0.9 confidence. Note that the prediction-markets dashboard shows a separate NetEase AI target of $147.61 with 18.33% upside, a small discrepancy suggesting the model is sensitive to Q2 earnings assumptions. Alibaba offers greater upside to the analyst consensus and a longer runway if AI cloud monetization continues to accelerate. Winner: Alibaba.

Alibaba is running hot. Shares are up 11.5% over the past month and 5.6% over one year, though year to date is −13.0%, with a beta of 0.51. Does Arista Networks (ANET) Have the Potential to Rally 26.33% as Wall Street Analysts Expect?
sum: Arista Networks (ANET) closed the last trading session at $188.67, gaining 0.9% over the past four weeks, but there could be plenty of upside left in the stock if short-term price targets set by Wall Street analysts are any guide. The mean price target of $238.34 indicates a 26.3% upside potential.

The average comprises 24 short-term price targets ranging from a low of $179.15 to a high of $289.00, with a standard deviation of $27.19. While the lowest estimate indicates a decline of 5.1% from the current price level, the most optimistic estimate points to a 53.2% upside. More than the range, one should note the standard deviation here, as it helps understand the variability of the estimates. The smaller the standard deviation, the greater the agreement among analysts.

While the consensus price target is highly sought after by investors, the ability and unbiasedness of analysts in setting price targets have long been questionable. And investors making investment decisions solely based on this tool would arguably do themselves a disservice.

However, an impressive consensus price target is not the only factor that indicates a potential upside in ANET. This view is strengthened by the agreement among analysts that the company will report better earnings than what they estimated earlier. Though a positive trend in earnings estimate revisions doesn't give any idea as to how much the stock could surge, it has proven effective in predicting an upside.

According to researchers at several universities across the globe, a price target is one of many pieces of information about a stock that misleads investors far more often than it guides. In fact, empirical research shows that price targets set by several analysts, irrespective of the extent of agreement, rarely indicate where the price of a stock could actually be heading.

While Wall Street analysts have deep knowledge of a company's fundamentals and the sensitivity of its business to economic and industry issues, many of them tend to set overly optimistic price targets. Are you wondering why?
They usually do that to drum up interest in shares of companies that their firms either have existing business relationships with or are looking to be associated with.

Eneba Partners with Marvel Rivals Publisher as Official NetEase Pay Gift Card Distributor
sum: VILNIUS, Lithuania, July 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Eneba, the fastest-growing digital entertainment marketplace, has become an official distributor of NetEase Pay gift cards. NetEase Pay is a service from NetEase Games, one of the world's leading game publishers. The partnership enables Eneba to offer NetEase Pay gift cards to its global audience.

Users will be pleased to find gift cards in various USD denominations and enjoy instant delivery after the purchase. The received digital code can be redeemed through the NetEase Games Club, where the balance can be used for eligible in-game purchases across more than 20 supported titles.

The NetEase Games lineup features many of the gaming industry's best-known titles, such as Marvel Rivals and Where Winds Meet. Marvel Rivals surpassed 10 million registered users within 72 hours of launch and exceeded 40 million by February 2025. Where Winds Meet recorded more than 3 million PC downloads within four days in China alone, reached over 15 million PC and mobile players within two weeks, and has since grown to more than 80 million players worldwide.

"What makes this partnership especially valuable is its global relevance," said Ignas Ivaškevičius, Category & Partnerships Manager at Eneba. "It deepens Eneba's position in a key Asian market while giving players around the world a simple way to purchase trusted, publisher-backed NetEase Pay gift cards."

For NetEase Pay, this partnership adds Eneba as an official distribution channel across international markets. It also reflects the importance of Asia as a shared strategic region for both companies. For users worldwide, this collaboration creates an easy way to purchase official NetEase Pay gift cards on Eneba for all their favorite NetEase Games titles.

Founded in 2018, Eneba is a digital entertainment marketplace trusted by more than 20 million registered users worldwide. The platform offers over 130,000 digital products, including games, game keys, gift cards, mobile top-ups, software, and subscriptions.
NetEase Pay is part of NetEase Games, the online games division of NetEase, Inc., one of the world's leading game developers and publishers.

items.t: Hang Seng Tech Index Plunges Over 3%; Tencent, NetEase Tumble More Than 7%; Gold Miners Surge Over 15%
sum: Hong Kong's stock market experienced violent turbulence on July 22, with the technology sector becoming the hardest-hit area. The Hang Seng Tech Index tumbled more than 3%, while gold and resource stocks surged against the trend, driven by escalating geopolitical risks and heightened risk-aversion sentiment, creating an extremely pronounced market divergence.

At the close, the Hang Seng Index settled at 24,892 points, down 239 points or 0.95%, losing the 25,000-point threshold. Full-day turnover reached HK$312.76 billion (approximately $39.9 billion). The China Enterprises Index also weakened, closing at 8,251 points, down 1.31%. The worst performer was the Hang Seng Tech Index, which plunged 146 points or 3.04% to 4,668 points.

Heavyweight tech stocks faced broad-based selling, becoming the primary drag on the broader market. Market reports indicated that Tencent Holdings (00700.HK) and NetEase (09999.HK) suffered severe blows, with single-day declines exceeding 7%. Tencent Holdings closed down 7.05%, with analysts attributing this closely to sector rotation. Data showed that Tencent was the most heavily reduced stock by mainland China's public funds in the previous quarter. NetEase tumbled 7.39%.

Other internet giants were not spared. Kuaishou (01024.HK) plunged 5.32%, while Bilibili dropped more than 4%. Alibaba (09988.HK), Xiaomi (01810.HK), Baidu (09888.HK), and JD.com (09618.HK) all recorded declines exceeding 2%, reflecting a heavy bearish market atmosphere.

Artificial intelligence and large model concept stocks also faced a cold spell. The previously sought-after duo, Minimax (00100.HK) and Zhipu (02513.HK), both retreated. Minimax crashed 11.42% for the day, while Zhipu pulled back after surging nearly 37% the previous day, closing down 3.61%. Reports indicated that JPMorgan recently issued a note stating that Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 had reshaped the valuation framework for large models, consequently lowering Zhipu's target price to 1,600 yuan, which exerted some pressure on market sentiment.

Semiconductor and chip stocks also mostly declined. SG Micro dropped more than 11%, APT Electronics fell over 10%, GigaDevice (03986.HK) and Hua Hong Semiconductor (01347.HK) both declined more than 4%, and bellwether SMIC (00981.HK) also reversed to fall 3.44%.

Texas Instruments or ServiceNow: One Stock Has the Analyst Conviction to Soar After Earnings
sum: Texas Instruments and ServiceNow both report earnings on the same day after weeks of steep selloffs, and Wall Street is quietly stacking its chips heavily toward one of them while the other faces a very different kind of pressure.
This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.

With Texas Instruments (NASDAQ:TXN | TXN Price Prediction) and ServiceNow (NYSE:NOW) both reporting Q2 2026 results after market close on Wednesday, July 22, 2026, the question for investors is simple: which name is Wall Street actually leaning into ahead of the same-session report? Both stocks slipped heading into Wednesday’s earnings report, with Texas Instruments off 4.9% and ServiceNow down 5.9% over the past week. Below is the head-to-head across the three dimensions that matter most going into Wednesday.

Wall Street’s rating distribution tells very different stories. Texas Instruments carries 17 Buy ratings, 17 Hold ratings, and two Sell ratings, a genuinely split book that reflects lingering questions about semiconductor cyclicality and the pace of the industrial recovery.

ServiceNow’s coverage is far more one-sided. Analysts have posted 43 Buy ratings, four Hold ratings, and one Sell rating, an overwhelmingly bullish tilt built around the agentic AI thesis and Now Assist net new ACV more than doubling year over year in the most recent quarter.
Texas Instruments closed at $284.07 on July 20 against an analyst consensus target of $303.59. That is a modest cushion, and with a P/E of 49, the multiple leaves little margin for a guide-down.

ServiceNow, by contrast, trades at $104.70 against an analyst target of $141.64. The gap is dramatically wider on a relative basis. NOW has been punished this year, down 31.7% year to date and 45.7% over the past year, while Texas Instruments has surged 65.7% year to date. The compressed ServiceNow valuation, at a P/E of 61, gives analysts more headroom to defend.

US Stocks Open Slightly Higher; SK Hynix Leads Chip and Memory Sector Rebound, Surges Over 4%
sum: US stocks opened moderately higher on Monday, with the chip and memory sector staging a strong rebound after recent volatility. South Korean memory giant SK Hynix led the charge, lifting overall market sentiment. Meanwhile, popular China-concept stocks also displayed robust upward momentum during pre-market trading.

As of 9:31 PM Eastern Time on July 20, all three major US indices opened slightly higher. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.30%, the S&P 500 gained 0.56%, and the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite outperformed with a 0.83% advance. This trajectory extended the optimistic tone set during the pre-market session, when all three index futures were already in positive territory — Dow futures up 0.12%, Nasdaq 100 futures up 0.42%, and S&P 500 futures up 0.23%.

From a sector perspective, semiconductor and memory chip stocks emerged as the biggest highlight after Monday's opening bell. Following pressure in the prior session, the sector saw significant capital inflows.

Specifically, SK Hynix shares gapped higher and maintained strength, surging more than 4% at one point before settling near a 4.15% gain, making it one of the most eye-catching chip stocks during the opening phase. Micron Technology followed closely, with shares rising 3.99%. According to NetEase reports, during pre-market trading, SK Hynix had already gained over 3%, Micron Technology rose over 2%, while SanDisk, Western Digital, Seagate Technology, Qualcomm, Intel, and Marvell Technology — among other storage and semiconductor-related names — generally advanced more than 1%.

As regular trading commenced, gains in chip stocks broadened further. Graphics processor giant Nvidia rose 1.5%, with its core position in AI computing power continuing to attract buyers. Contract chipmaking leader TSMC gained 1.85%, and communications chip giant Broadcom advanced 2.25%. In the processor space, AMD delivered a strong performance with a 3.54% gain, while Intel also rose 2.63%.

Semiconductor equipment manufacturers were similarly boosted. Dutch lithography giant ASML saw its shares rise 2.19%, while US semiconductor equipment leader Lam Research gained 2.76%. Additionally, chip design architecture company ARM rose 2.27%, and SanDisk built on its pre-market momentum to climb 3.78% after the opening bell.

items.t: NetEase stock highlights stronger game revenue in Q2
sum: NetEase stock (ISIN US64110W1027) generated CNY 30.1 billion in second-quarter 2026 revenue, with online games revenue rising 10 percent year over year to CNY 24.5 billion. The figures give investors a mixed earnings picture because revenue expanded while adjusted profit declined.

According to Yahoo Finance in the August 20, 2026 earnings call, total revenue reached CNY 30.1 billion in Q2, while games and related value-added services produced CNY 25.0 billion, up 10 percent year over year. Online games revenue increased 10 percent year over year, although it fell 2 percent from the prior quarter as some self-developed and licensed titles softened.

The company also reported CNY 60.7 billion in revenue for the first half of 2026, a 7 percent year-over-year increase. That mix places the games portfolio at the center of the investment case, while the sequential decline shows why upcoming releases and live-service updates remain important for growth.

Yahoo Finance reported that NetEase's non-GAAP net income attributable to shareholders was CNY 7.7 billion in Q2, with the decline attributed primarily to investment losses. Non-GAAP basic earnings were USD 1.78 per ADS, or USD 0.36 per share.

Gross profit margin moved to 70.5 percent in Q2 from 64.7 percent in the prior-year period. Games and related value-added services posted a 76.1 percent margin, compared with 70.2 percent a year earlier, making margin expansion a counterweight to the lower profit figure.

NetEase also reported a CNY 157.5 billion net cash position as of June 30, 2026, compared with CNY 163.5 billion at the end of 2025. The balance sheet gives the company room to fund new content and shareholder returns, but the lower cash figure adds a measurable counter-factor.

According to MarketBeat on October 1, 2026, seven analysts rated NetEase Buy and three rated it Hold, producing a Moderate Buy consensus and an average price target of USD 163.62. The target lies 37.4 percent above the stock price of USD 119.07, a gap that reflects expectations for continued game growth rather than the latest profit decline.

How Thatgamecompany and NetEase grew Sky's community in China
sum: - In China, Sky: Children of the Light draws one of its most devoted audiences anywhere - and SJ Xue says the reason has little to do with money.
- Having sat on both sides of East-West dealmaking, first at NetEase, now at Thatgamecompany, Xue explains what actually determines whether a cross-border partnership succeeds.
- Capital and market entry only get a deal started: it's trust, shared craft and mutual respect between teams that really matters, according to Xue.
Cross-border deals are usually sold on funding and market entry, but that's rarely what makes them last.

Ahead of his PGC Summit Shanghai panel on publishing in China on July 29th, SJ Xue, head of corporate development at Thatgamecompany, talks to PocketGamer.biz about partnering with NetEase on Sky: Children of the Light and why trust between the teams matters more than anything written into the terms.

PocketGamer.biz: Most East-meets-West conversations are framed as Western studios trying to crack China. Your experience runs the other way - working with NetEase as the partner helping you grow. What does that relationship actually look like day-to-day and what surprised you most about how it works?

SJ: I've had the unique opportunity to experience this partnership from both sides. Before joining Thatgamecompany, I spent several years at NetEase where I was part of the team that invested in the studio.
